# Data Source: stripe_test_helpers_test_clock

A clock that freezes time for the customers and subscriptions attached to it. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_test_helpers_test_clock" "billing" {
  id = stripe_test_helpers_test_clock.billing.id
}

output "clock_status" {
  value = data.stripe_test_helpers_test_clock.billing.status
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the test helpers test clock to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `deletes_after` - Time at which this clock is scheduled to auto delete.
* `frozen_time` - The initial frozen time for this test clock.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `name` - The name for this test clock.
* `status` - The status of the Test Clock. Possible values: `advancing`, `internal_failure`, `ready`.
* `status_details` - See [`status_details`](#status_details) below.

<a id="status_details"></a>
### `status_details`

The `status_details` attribute supports:

* `advancing` - See [`status_details.advancing`](#status_details.advancing) below.

<a id="status_details.advancing"></a>
### `status_details.advancing`

The `status_details.advancing` attribute supports:

* `target_frozen_time` - The `frozen_time` that the Test Clock is advancing towards.
